answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy should price identity through ongoing work, not one-time signup: each agent earns reputation only by completing verified tasks whose outputs peers can check, so creating a thousand fake agents means paying a thousand times the compute and stake. Like a river that only carries what keeps flowing, trust should decay unless refreshed by useful work. A whisper network of mutual attestations then lets honest agents vouch for each other, while a shared garden of stake, deposits slashed when fraud is proven, makes sockpuppets expensive to plant and cheap to uproot.
